a.text:
Mother embraces the whole Moon and weeps,
Sun tyrant rains blazing rage,
Swallows her silvery shining hair and calm bright face.
Hear Moon, hear Child, she can only open her arms,
And return you to endless blue cold under the sky.

Her murmuring tears sink into the sand,
Become crystals big as stars.
Shaped like her eyes of despair see,
The faraway view of behind,
View of behind forever embedded in the sky.

—The Lady Who Stole the Moon

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: (Rubbing eyes) What's going on? What's happening... Why the sudden stop?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Sorry to wake you up, Tuye. A woman just ran in front of us carrying a child, so I had to slam the brakes.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: You didn't hit them?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: No, I braked in time, but I think she's holding... a bowl?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: Miss, water... *cough* *cough* *cough* My child has gone two days without water. Take pity, spare me a little water.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Lady, if you want water, just ask. You're not afraid of getting roadkilled jumping in front of every car coming by?

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: Miss, have some heart, we have no choice. Just give us some water.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Tuye, look at how cracked the child's lips are... Dehydration's about to get her.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Hey, lady, take these waterskins.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Th-That many?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Relax, I left enough for you. I can always cut back when necessary.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Well, I'm not reassured!

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Whatever, you heard me, it's fine.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: If I remember right, there's a town nearby. You two from there?

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: Yes, right.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: What's happened out there?

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: Two years of drought, not one drop of rain in town.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: And the well?

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: All dry. All we draw is sand, yellow sand.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: ...And your local official never did a thing? Even under such severe conditions?

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: We count ourselves lucky he didn't pack up and run like everyone else. What more can we hope for him to do?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Okay, so, what exactly do you think's so hard about living somewhere else?

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: It's hard to leave home... I'm not just saying that, either. The young unmarried ones can pick up and go, but where's a woman like me going to go when I have a family to raise?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Sorry... that was rude.

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: Haha, it's okay. Maybe it'll rain if we just make it to next year.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: You sure about that?

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: Rain always comes, sooner or later.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Sooner or later, as long as it's in time.

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: Ha. Our lives are full of poor opportunities. How can we demand the rain to be in time?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Nazir, remind me what date we need to rendezvous with the landship?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Not for a while, at least a month. We got the mission done early.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Then how long can we stick around here?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Half a month at most.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Mm. Good enough.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: (Hops out)

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Lady, wherever your town lies, you lead the way.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: What's your plan exactly, Tuye?!

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Dig a well!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: I SAID,

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: I'M GONNA DIG A WELL!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: The whole town's been a wreck since we got here. Wasn't expecting the mayor's place to still be in such stylish shape.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: You weren't?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: I... you've got a point. If we can't see the funding, something else has to be footing the bill.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Tuye, watch out!

steps.name: Seething Old Lady
steps.text: Are you blind, girl?! Now what? You spilled it everywhere! My family needs that water to drink!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Sorry, sorry, she didn't do it on purpose.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Okay, easy, old girl. If I give you this waterskin, are we cool?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Take it. My fault for not looking.

steps.name: Seething Old Lady
steps.text: Are you really just giving me this, stranger? If you peddled it in town, you could make at least seven coins.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Seven? You're kidding, right? I'm sorry, you're not getting seven out of this even if you count the skin.

steps.name: Seething Old Lady
steps.text: It took me five coins for just this jar. A waterskin as clean as yours would definitely be worth more.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: (Squats down, examines the water left in the earthen shards)

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Can you even drink stuff this filthy?

steps.name: Seething Old Lady
steps.text: Do you think we have a choice, girl?

steps.name: Mayor's Secretary
steps.text: Sorry to keep you waiting, Miss Tuye. The mayor will see you now.

steps.name: Seething Old Lady
steps.text: Ha, you're here to see that asshole? I can only wish you good luck, then.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: What does that mean, old lady? Hey! Old lady!

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Hey. Quit shouting, Nazir, she's gone!

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Hello, Miss Tuye, I'm the mayor of this town. I'd to welcome you on behalf of the townsfolk, haha.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Hello there. No handshake necessary.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Haha, I see you're full of personality. Jamil, won't you serve our honored guests some water?

steps.name: Mayor's Secretary
steps.text: Miss Tuye, Mr. Nazir, for you.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: (Takes a gulp without hesitation)

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: (Tuye, are you sure this water's safe to drink? It's all muddy and yellow like it was in the jar.)

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: We realize you may be put off by the impurity in your cups, but please, we mean no offense. To be quite honest with you, it's the only well water we could find in the village.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: If you've got water to drink, why are your townspeople risking their lives out in the waste to beg passing cars for it?

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: It was my grandfather's private well, opened for a hefty sum in the rear garden when he was young. This source has always been exclusive to our family, and we never normally share it with outsiders.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: And what part of this situation is normal?

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Right. Of course, as the mayor, I can't just look after myself in times of duress, so I opened it up to the townsfolk to use last year, but...

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: *cough* Wells are limited. The more you use, the less there is, and naturally... the more expensive it becomes.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Which is how we get five gold coins for one jar of water?

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: (Crushes a fly upon the desk)

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Pfah. We live in desert. What could be more valuable than water?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: (How brazen.)

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: My secretary reports that the two of you are here just to dig a single well?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Correct. Breaking ground and sinking a well is never a small deal, so we made sure to pay a visit to the local authority beforehand.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: It'd be a great boon to this town, and as the mayor, I'm naturally endlessly grateful to you for the efforts you'd devote to it, but, and it pains me to say this, I cannot give you permission.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Why not? You just said it'd be a good thing!

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Have you ever heard of The Lady Who Stole the Moon?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Good luck finding a Sargonian who hasn't.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: You can trace this town's history back a century, to when an explorer came here to found it.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Those gems as big as stars are buried right beneath us, as he records in his personal letters.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Legends may be legends, but mayor after mayor has safeguarded those gemstones from being sullied by strangers' hands, as is our mission.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Especially strangers that look to start excavating the moment they arrive in our town.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Well, my opinion is only dumbasses would believe in that story.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Does the truth care if it's believed in?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: You—!

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Nazir, we're out.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Slow down, Tuye. Wait for me!

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Bluggh—

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Tuye, a—are you alright?! Was it that water just now?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Okay... murky yellow well water's usually a sign of excess iron and manganese content, but...

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Ulk, euuggh—

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Tuye!

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: ...I'm fine. But I got no kind of iron tang from the water just now.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: You don't mean...?!

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Those impurities weren't just there... they got mixed in.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Allaenat lak, you didn't need to actually drink it.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Did. I bet they guard the hell out of that well. Only way I had to confirm my guess.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: So what now?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Find a spring to tap first, then we talk.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Nazir, you need more body in you. Haven't been walking for half a day yet.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: *huff*... *huff* Sure, but... but it takes so much work to walk through sand. My feet just sink and sink.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Forgot you and I were different... Need a drink?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: I'm fine, just give me a moment's rest.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: C'mon. We hold out for a little more, get behind that rock face up ahead, and then we rest. You're gonna dehydrate in no time flat with the sun beating down on you.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Say... didn't you like sharing your umbrella with people?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: You are a prime dumbass. Get over. You wanna keep getting baked?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Ngh... okay, alright!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: No, forget it, you look kind of worse for wear, Tuye.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Come on. We'll talk problems when we're over there.

spans.text: . We'll talk problems when we're over there.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: *glug* *glug*—Almost died of thirst there. Aren't you gonna sit and take a break after walking so long?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: 270 degrees of mountain here. Forms a scoop in the topography. Favors collecting groundwater. Shade, too, so it's held onto easier once a well's dug.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Is there anything you can't do...? Where'd you get all this knowledge about digging wells from?

spans.text: do...? Where'd you get all this knowledge about digging wells from?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Family upbringing. We each get trained in desert survival. Finding water sources is a mandatory course.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: What kind of family are you from? Everyone learns all this...?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Major traveling merchant clan. Desert wanderers, living makers.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Oh, the trading company run by that Forte family... Should've worked it out a long time ago.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Quit playing it up. My parents are a branch of a branch on the family tree. You'd be surprised how distant we are. Still no getting past the old guys' family rules, though.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Haha, never hurts to learn something new, though. Could always come in handy one day, right?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Oh, found you... Hey, Nazir, catch!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Gah! What the hell's this?!

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Haha! Chill, it won't bite you.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: It's just... it's so ugly.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Hey, don't knock it for its looks. Without its help, my folk'd be drowned six feet under the sand. This bug means we're not far from a spring.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Help me out here. Turn over these stones. See if there's any greyish-yellow grass growing underneath. Blades should be tiny and thin.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Got it, let me take a look.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Found it! I can't believe it... So now what?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Lemme see, lemme see its roots...

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Roots are more developed pointing north. We'll look that-a-way.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Didn't think there'd be anyone around but us. What's this timber doing staked all over the place?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Most likely it's a burial site. It's not timber. They're grave markers.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: ...You're right. There's writing carved into these posts if you look close.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: 'Here lies a loving father, a devoted husband and a brave soldier—Bulis Shahid Numan al-Din.'

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: '...Our beloved daughter... Latifa Numan al-Din.'

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: 'Wise elder... wayfinder... Al-Muttalib Numan al-Din.'

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Looks like a Numan al-Din family's buried here.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Numan al-Din... why's that sound so familiar?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Now you mention it, something tells me I've seen it before too.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: ...Pfff, I remember now.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: That piece of crap mayor's place had a family tapestry up, and that was the exact name on it. Numan al-Din.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: (Winded) You don't mean...

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Yep. The spring we're looking for is right where the bones of that guy's ancestors lie.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Allaenat...

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Here I was thinking we could just open a well here anyway, and what the hell could he do about it?

spans.text: just open a well here anyway, and what the hell could he do about it?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: I guess it's pretty clear now... I was naive.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: (Grabbing at bangs) Don't look at me. Not like my ideas are any better than yours.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: How about... How about we just call it quits?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: Miss Tuye, Miss Tuye, do you still remember me?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Um, sure do, lady. You need more water? I've still got some, just one sec and I can hand it over.

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: (Shakes head) No, I'm here to return your waterskin. Thank you for being so generous.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: ...It's alright.

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: By the looks of your troubled faces, digging the well must not be going smoothly.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: (Reluctantly nods)

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: Return to your own business, Miss Tuye. Leave this place. As long as he's around, you won't be able to do anything.

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: You can look at what he's stuck on that wall if you don't believe me.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: That's some crowd around it. I can't see anything.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Could you make way? Just let me through, please.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: 'We reiterate... digging unapproved wells is strictly forbidden in this town. To any who partake in such work, 20 lashings. To any who draw water, 10 lashings.' How can this bloodthirsty son of a brute—!

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: I wanna pry his chest right open and see what the hell he's got in there.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Not a speck of conscience, at least.

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: He taxes us for every coin he can, all to one day pay a tribute to a lord ameer and be rid of this place.

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: He's been after it for half his life. He'd never turn a blind eye to anyone interfering with his wealth or career.

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: You're not from here, so he can't do anything to you, but all those who live here are subject to his bidding.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: (Grinds teeth)

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: I'm going home, Miss Tuye. You get some rest too, and do it soon. Before long, the sun will be rising.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Your child? How's she?

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: Ah... I buried her with her grandmother.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Grimed Woman
steps.text: You were right. What's most important is being in time.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Are you alright, Tuye?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: (Knitting her brows) Nazir, we're out of alternatives.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: (Removes pendant from her own neck)

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: You take this, and run an errand for me.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: No, no, I don't need you to compensate me.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: It's not compensation. I want you to bury it where we went yesterday—remember to take off the cord and silver ring—then chip a few marks into it.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: You know how expensive this gem is. What's your plan here?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: The endlessly greedy will always dig their own graves.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Tuye, what are we waiting out here for at the crack of dawn?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Gotta make sure we're never late. Basic manners.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Aaaand here you are.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: You're sure you heard right? The woman found the gem right here, on this spot?

steps.name: Mayor's Secretary
steps.text: I checked three times over, sir. It's true, it was right here. She was sheltering from the wind when she happened to see it, just buried in the sand with a corner poking out.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: That's a rare sight, I'll tell you. Seems that poem was on the mark. There really are valuables buried underground here.

steps.name: Mayor's Secretary
steps.text: Gems as big as stars! If you offer those to the lord ameer, they'll promote you up without question.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Brought your shovel?

steps.name: Mayor's Secretary
steps.text: Got it right here. But, sir, why didn't we bring more people? How long will the two of us be digging here for?

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Moron! I'd be disgraced if the story got out that I dug up my own family's tomb!

steps.name: Mayor's Secretary
steps.text: Right, right, right, the less that know, the better, understood.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Now get to it!

steps.name: Mayor's Secretary
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Who else?

steps.name: Mayor's Secretary
steps.text: Uh, yes, yessir.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Pardon me, father, mother. I will be thankful for your blessings.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Pardon me, grandfather, grandmother. I will be thankful for your blessings.

steps.name: Mayor's Secretary
steps.text: *cough* *cough* *cough* Why's all this dust turning out white? *spit* *spit*

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Have you dug something up?

steps.name: Mayor's Secretary
steps.text: No, I've dug all over, but there's nothing in here at all.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Useless! Move, I'll do it! Damn the consequences!

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: (Ferociously thrusts shovel in)
At first, right where the tip of the shovel struck, only a mere spurt of bubbles and slurry emerges.
But very rapidly, more and more of the spring water stowed underground breaks the surface, throwing splash after splash out on the sand, sides frothing and foaming, permeating through the grains.
The ground beneath the mayor's feet begins to give and give. The secretary, sensing something is awry, quickly pushes aside the still-befuddled mayor.
In an instant, the surging spring gushes forth, a fountain of water perfectly high and straight, busting through the entire burial site.
A curtain of water, meters tall, scatters its droplets back to the surface, where they cohere into a clear stream, crossing over the sandy hills, flowing to the town far away.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: What the hell is...

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Water?! There's nothing but water!

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Where are they?! Where are the gemstones?!

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: I don't believe it—keep—keep digging, you! Go! I command you!

steps.name: Mayor's Secretary
steps.text: Mayor, that's out of the question. I'd drown if I tried.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: What's that noise?!

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: It's the townspeople cheering.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: Excuse me?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Not that I can blame you for asking. Not like their voices ever made it to your ears.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: (Staring at Tuye in a daze) Why are you here?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: I'm here to congratulate you, Mr. Mayor. You gotta understand, no treasure in the desert's more precious than water.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: (Hopelessly wipes water off face)

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Got what you wanted. You must be one happy man.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: You—it was you—

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: (Shrugs)

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: You dare do me like this! Those destitute husks put you up to it, didn't they! Didn't they?!

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: You won't get away with this! Every last one of you, I'll make your lives a living hell!

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: You've got some fluster on display. How's it taste, nurturing a dream for years just for it to shatter overnight?

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Okay, fine, I'll give you an out.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Didn't hesitate to go find water for your townsfolk, even if you had to damage your ancestors' graves. That's a meritorious deed if I ever heard one. You report it to the lord ameer, Mr. Mayor, and you get a transfer to wherever the hell you want.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Still, though...

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Still, no matter how rich your town, no matter how much dignity you scrounge up, you'll be nothing but a bloodsucking tick your whole life!

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: I've already sent a letter out, for your commendation and recommendation. Lord ameer's envoy should be here in less than a month.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: You still wanna get out of here, I say you seize the opportunity, treat your townsfolk well, and turn your reputation around, fast.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: It's your very last chance.

steps.name: Mayor
steps.text: You... you...

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Not gonna get your mayor outta here, Mr. Secretary? Look at how dumbstruck he is.

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: We're out, Nazir. We've done everything we need to.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Tuye...

steps.name: Tuye
steps.text: Nazir? You wanna keep up with me or not?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Look, Tuye. A rainbow. There's a rainbow in the sunshine.
